principles: Only activate advisory playbooks from explicit evidence, never from DONE success alone.
Keep the workflow host-neutral and command-layer neutral.
Preserve fail-closed digest, lineage, and harmful-signal guards.
Do not add broad automation just to remove a manual step.
Prove the user-facing CLI transcript, not just internal handler calls.
drivers: The user rejected hidden default-off or human-memory-dependent activation as fake closure.
Existing activation guards already know how to verify outcomes, lineage, recommendation, and candidate digest.
Historical backfill and daemon/timer rollout are explicitly out of Story 2 scope.

options.name: auto-apply writes deterministic recommendation before activation
pros: Removes the separate default-off promotion_sweep apply step for candidates that already meet activation evidence thresholds.
Keeps activation guarded by the same aggregate digest, candidate digest, lineage, exposure, and harmful-signal checks.
Can be proven in one CLI transcript with playbook_auto_promotion_apply --apply and runtime consumption verify.
cons: Requires careful idempotency so recommendation rows are not duplicated.
Must ensure dry-run remains read-only and does not silently promote.

options.name: require separate promotion_sweep apply then activation apply
pros: Minimal code change because current primitives already exist.
cons: Still leaves the workflow dependent on a manually remembered default-off step.
Does not satisfy the user requirement to avoid fake/off-by-default closure.

options.name: timer-driven activation worker
pros: Might reduce operator action after enough data exists.
cons: Too broad for this story and explicitly out of scope.
Adds lifecycle risk before proving the single evidence path.

chosen: auto-apply writes deterministic recommendation before activation
rationale: Choose the smallest real correctness/product fix: playbook_auto_promotion_apply --apply should create the missing deterministic recommend_activate evidence for already-qualified candidates, then activate through the existing guarded audit path. This removes the fake default-off/manual step while preserving fail-closed evidence boundaries.

preMortem.scenario: Auto apply activates from DONE settlement or neutral rows.
preMortem.trigger: Outcome filtering treats done-settlement or exposureMode none as helped evidence.
preMortem.consequence: Playbook becomes active without real candidate consumption proof.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep isCandidateConsumedPlaybookOutcome and verdictSource != done-settlement checks load-bearing in smoke.

preMortem.scenario: Recommendation row is written but candidate digest changes before activation.
preMortem.trigger: Candidate mutates between decision construction and apply write.
preMortem.consequence: Stale recommendation authorizes a different playbook body.
preMortem.mitigation: Bind recommendation to aggregateDigest and playbookDigest, then re-read and verify candidate digest before status write.

preMortem.scenario: Second apply duplicates decisions or activation audit rows.
preMortem.trigger: Idempotency key does not include stable candidate/evidence/policy digest fields.
preMortem.consequence: Learning store gets noisy and future audit cannot tell what happened.
preMortem.mitigation: Reuse deterministic idempotency keys and assert second apply activatedCount=0 with one activation audit row.

preMortem.scenario: Docs imply playbooks are gate evidence or production policy.
preMortem.trigger: Activation wording says automatic without advisory/non-authoritative boundary.
preMortem.consequence: Users over-trust memory advice as proof.
preMortem.mitigation: Docs and delivery check must state advisory, non-authoritative, no gate evidence, and no blocking policy.
